svg.text: NP-Completeness & Computational Complexity
Complexity Classes
• P: problems solvable in polynomial time O(nᵏ) deterministically
• NP: problems verifiable in polynomial time given a certificate
→ not "non-polynomial" — Non-deterministic Polynomial
• NP-hard: at least as hard as every problem in NP
• NP-complete: in NP AND NP-hard (hardest problems in NP)
• P ⊆ NP — whether P = NP is the biggest open problem in CS
• co-NP: complement of NP (verify NO instances in poly time)
Polynomial Reductions
• A ≤ₚ B: A reduces to B — solving B solves A
• If B ∈ P and A ≤ₚ B then A ∈ P
• If B is NP-hard and B ≤ₚ C then C is NP-hard
• Cook-Levin theorem: SAT is NP-complete (first proof, 1971)
• Reduction chain: SAT → 3-SAT → Independent Set → Clique
→ Vertex Cover → Hamiltonian Cycle → TSP
• To prove X NP-hard: reduce known NP-hard problem Y to X
Classic NP-Complete Problems
• SAT / 3-SAT: satisfiability of boolean formula
• Independent Set: largest set of non-adjacent vertices
• Vertex Cover: smallest set covering all edges
• Clique: largest complete subgraph
• Hamiltonian Cycle: cycle visiting every vertex once
• TSP (decision): tour of cost ≤ k? (optimization: find min tour)
• Graph k-Coloring (k ≥ 3): is χ(G) ≤ k?
• Subset Sum: does subset of integers sum to target T?
Coping Strategies for NP-Hard Problems
• Exact algorithms for small n: branch-and-bound, dynamic programming
→ TSP: O(n² 2ⁿ) DP (Held-Karp), feasible for n ≤ 20
• Approximation algorithms: PTAS, FPTAS, constant-factor approx
→ TSP with triangle inequality: 2-approximation (Christofides 1.5x)
→ Vertex Cover: 2-approximation via maximal matching
• Fixed-parameter tractable (FPT): O(f(k) × nᶜ) where k is parameter
• Heuristics: simulated annealing, genetic algorithms, local search
• Special cases: many NP-hard problems are poly on restricted inputs
P ⊆ NP — P=NP? unsolved
SAT: first NP-complete (Cook 1971)
Prove NP-hard: reduce known → target
TSP approx: 1.5x (Christofides)
Vertex Cover: 2-approximation
